action: As the town urges residents (relayed by ZATAZ): watch bank transactions, change reused passwords, turn on two-factor authentication where possible and beware of fraudulent calls and messages.
exec: A small municipality fell back to paper after an attack, and a ransomware group now claims it and has posted documents it says are the town's.
impact: IT network shut down as a precaution; municipal services largely on paper with slower processing; reception, phone and website still working.
plain: The town hall of Chambourcy, near Paris, was hit by a cyberattack over the weekend of November 7-8 and turned off its network. A ransomware group says it did it and posted sample documents.
summary: The town hall of Chambourcy (Yvelines) reported a cyberattack over the weekend of 7-8 November and shut its IT network as a precaution; most services moved to paper. It filed a complaint and informed the CNIL (InfoSyvelines, ZATAZ). ZATAZ reports that the INC Ransom group claimed the intrusion on 19 November and posted document samples it presents as municipal files; ZATAZ does not report the town confirming the group's claim.
title: Chambourcy town hall in France hit by cyberattack, services moved to paper; INC Ransom claims it

validation.note: InfoSyvelines (10 Nov) and ZATAZ (23 Nov) each report the town hall confirming the attack, the preventive shutdown, paper mode, complaint and CNIL notice. The INC Ransom claim (19 Nov, document samples) is reported by ZATAZ only and is the group's claim; the town's own notice on chambourcy.fr was not read.

date_note: Attack over the weekend of 7-8 November; InfoSyvelines published on 10 November (last modified 12 November). Added later than the map window.
